QUESTION: What is the mileage rate for business travel?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
The mileage rate for business travel is 55 pence per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year, and 25 pence per mile thereafter. [HR-13#001]

EVIDENCE:
[HR-13#001] Expenses Policy > Mileage (v2.0, effective 2026-04-01)
This policy replaces HR-03 with effect from 1 April 2026.

Employees using a private vehicle for business travel may claim 55 pence per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year, and 25 pence per mile thereafter. These rates match the HMRC approved mileage allowance payment rates that took effect on 6 April 2026, so no tax liability arises and no Mileage Allowance Relief is due.

Journeys between home and the normal place of work are not claimable. Where an employee travels from home directly to a customer site, the claimable distance is the lesser of the actual journey and the journey from the office.

---

[HR-03#001] Expenses Policy > Mileage; Meals (v1.3, effective 2024-04-01) [SUPERSEDED, replaced by HR-13]
> This version has been withdrawn. See HR-13 for the policy in force.

Employees using a private vehicle for business travel may claim 40 pence per mile. Journeys between home and the normal place of work are not claimable.

| Circumstance | Limit |
|---|---|
| Breakfast, where travel begins before 06:00 | £6 |
| Lunch, where away from site for more than 5 hours | £8 |
| Evening meal, where returning after 20:00 | £18 |

Alcohol is not reimbursed.

---

[HR-13#003] Expenses Policy > Accommodation (v2.0, effective 2026-04-01)
Hotel accommodation is capped at £130 per night outside London and £170 per night within the M25. Bookings must be made through the company travel portal. Where the cap cannot be met, prior approval from the department head is required.

---

[HR-03#002] Expenses Policy > Accommodation; Submission (v1.3, effective 2024-04-01) [SUPERSEDED, replaced by HR-13]
Hotel accommodation is capped at £110 per night outside London and £140 per night within the M25. Bookings must be made through the nominated travel agent wherever possible.

Claims are submitted on the paper expenses form with original receipts attached, and must reach Finance within 60 days of the expenditure. Claims are reimbursed with the following month's salary.

---

[GEN-01#003] Company Overview > Who we sell to; Structure (v1.4, effective 2026-01-15)
Roughly 70% of revenue comes from trade customers: independent restaurants, cafes, catering companies and small hotel groups, predominantly within a 60-mile radius of the site. The remaining 30% is direct-to-consumer through the online store.

The company has six departments: Sales, Customer Services, Warehouse and Logistics, Finance, IT, and People. Each department head reports to the Managing Director. The senior team meets weekly on Monday mornings.

---

[CS-11#002] Delivery Frequently Asked Questions > What does delivery cost? (v2.2, effective 2026-02-01)
| Service | Cost, excluding VAT |
|---|---|
| Standard, orders under £75 | £6.95 |
| Standard, orders £75 and over | Free |
| Next working day | £12.95 |
| Pre-noon next working day | £19.95 |
| Highlands, islands and Northern Ireland | £14.95, 3 to 7 working days |

Free delivery applies to the goods value excluding VAT and excluding any surcharge postcodes.

QUESTION: How quickly must I report a lost company laptop?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
You must report a lost company laptop to the IT helpdesk within 1 hour of becoming aware [IT-03#001].

EVIDENCE:
[IT-03#001] Security Incident Reporting > What counts as an incident (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Report any of the following:

- A lost or stolen laptop, phone or USB device
- An email sent to the wrong recipient containing personal or confidential data
- Clicking a link or opening an attachment in a suspected phishing email
- Suspected malware, ransomware or unexpected system behaviour
- Unauthorised access to a system, room or filing cabinet
- Paper records lost, or found where they should not be
- Any suspicion that a password has been compromised

If you are unsure whether something is an incident, report it. Reporting something harmless costs a few minutes; not reporting a real breach can cost the company a great deal more.

---

[IT-03#002] Security Incident Reporting > How to report; Timescales (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Telephone the IT helpdesk on extension 4040 immediately, and follow up by email to ithelp@northgate-kitchenware.invalid. Do not attempt to fix or investigate the problem yourself, and do not delete anything, as evidence may be needed.

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Report to IT helpdesk | Within 1 hour of becoming aware |
| IT initial assessment | Within 4 hours |
| Notify Data Protection Lead if personal data is involved | Within 24 hours |
| Notify the ICO if the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights | Within 72 hours of the company becoming aware |
| Notify affected individuals if the risk is high | Without undue delay |

---

[GEN-04#003] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Responsibilities (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment remains the property of Northgate Kitchenware Ltd. Staff are responsible for its reasonable care. Loss or theft must be reported to the IT helpdesk within 24 hours and, if the device held company data, this also triggers the security incident procedure in IT-03.

Personal use of company equipment is permitted within reason. Installing unlicensed software, disabling security software, or allowing family members to use a company device are not permitted.

---

[IT-02#003] Data Protection and Information Handling > Reporting a suspected breach; Access review (v2.0, effective 2025-11-01)
A suspected personal data breach is reported to the Data Protection Lead within 24 hours of discovery, whether or not it is later confirmed.

Access to systems holding personal data is reviewed annually by the Data Protection Lead. Managers confirm in writing that every account in their area is still required.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[IT-04#004] Backup and Recovery > Testing; Requesting a restore (v1.3, effective 2025-05-01)
A restore test is performed quarterly. One system is chosen at random, restored to an isolated environment, and verified. Results are recorded and reported to the senior team. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup.

Staff who need a deleted file recovered contact the IT helpdesk. Files deleted within the last 30 days can normally be recovered the same working day.

QUESTION: What is the timescale for reviewing accident records?

All accidents, injuries and near misses are recorded in the accident book. The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews each entry within five working days and determines whether it is reportable to the Health and Safety Executive.

The Health and Safety Coordinator conducts a documented site inspection monthly. Findings and outstanding actions are reported to the senior team. An external health and safety consultant audits the site annually.

---

[OPS-08#004] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Escalation; Investigation (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews every entry within two working days and decides whether it is reportable under RIDDOR 2013.

| Category | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Death or specified injury | Report to HSE without delay, then within 10 days |
| Over-seven-day incapacitation | Report within 15 days |
| Dangerous occurrence | Report without delay, then within 10 days |
| Occupational disease | Report on diagnosis |

Any accident causing injury, and any near miss with the potential to cause serious injury, is investigated by the Health and Safety Coordinator with the relevant supervisor. Findings and corrective actions are reported to the senior team monthly.

---

---

Every accident, injury and near miss must be recorded in the accident book held in the warehouse office, on the same day wherever possible. This includes incidents involving visitors and contractors, and incidents where no injury resulted.

---

[REG-02#003] Data Retention Schedule > Reporting a suspected breach; Disposal; Review (v1.8, effective 2025-11-01)
Suspected breaches of this schedule, including data retained past its period or disposed of early, are reported to the Data Protection Lead within 72 hours.

At the end of the retention period, electronic records are deleted, including from backups at the next backup cycle rollover, and paper records are cross-cut shredded. Disposal of confidential waste is carried out under a certificate of destruction.

Deletion is not performed where a record is subject to an ongoing legal claim, investigation or regulatory request. In that case the record is placed on legal hold and the reason recorded.

The Data Protection Lead reviews this schedule annually against current legislation.

---

[REG-01#003] Health and Safety Policy > Risk assessment (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Risk assessments are completed for all significant activities, reviewed annually, and reviewed immediately following an accident, a near miss, or a change to the activity. Assessments are held in the warehouse office and on the shared drive.

Specific assessments cover manual handling, workplace transport, working at height, display screen equipment, COSHH, and new and expectant mothers.

QUESTION: Can I use washing-up liquid when washing by hand?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [PRD-02#002], a small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan.

EVIDENCE:
[PRD-02#002] Cast Iron Care Guide > Everyday washing (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

[PRD-02#003] Cast Iron Care Guide > Stuck-on food; Rust (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Simmer a little water in the pan for a few minutes and scrape with a wooden spatula, or scour with coarse salt and a paper towel. Do not soak.

Rust is not a fault and is not covered by warranty. Scour the rust off with steel wool, wash, dry, and re-season from bare metal.

---

[PRD-01#004] Knife Care Guide > Storage; Stainless and carbon steel (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[PRD-02#001] Cast Iron Care Guide > Seasoning (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Seasoning is a layer of polymerised oil bonded to the iron. It gives the non-stick surface and protects against rust. It is built up, not applied once.

To season: wash and dry thoroughly, apply a very thin coat of a high smoke point oil such as rapeseed or grapeseed, wipe out until the surface looks dry, then bake upside down at 220°C for one hour with a tray beneath. Let it cool in the oven. Repeat two or three times for a new or stripped pan.

Too much oil is the most common mistake. It leaves a sticky, patchy surface rather than a hard one.

Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-02#004] Cast Iron Care Guide > What not to cook; Enamelled cast iron (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Highly acidic foods such as tomato sauce and wine reductions will strip a young seasoning if simmered for a long time. A well-established seasoning tolerates them.

Enamelled pans are not seasoned and must not be. Avoid thermal shock: never put a hot enamelled pan into cold water, as the enamel will craze.

---

[PRD-02#001] Cast Iron Care Guide > Seasoning (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Seasoning is a layer of polymerised oil bonded to the iron. It gives the non-stick surface and protects against rust. It is built up, not applied once.

To season: wash and dry thoroughly, apply a very thin coat of a high smoke point oil such as rapeseed or grapeseed, wipe out until the surface looks dry, then bake upside down at 220°C for one hour with a tray beneath. Let it cool in the oven. Repeat two or three times for a new or stripped pan.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

Northgate Kitchenware Ltd is committed to providing a safe and healthy working environment for employees, contractors, visitors and anyone affected by its activities, so far as is reasonably practicable. This policy is reviewed annually and is signed by the Managing Director.

Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.

Sharpen when the knife no longer slices a tomato skin cleanly under its own weight.

The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March.

Leave is requested through the People system at least two weeks before the intended start date for absences of up to five days, and at least six weeks before for longer absences. Requests are approved by the line manager.

Approval is not automatic. Managers must maintain adequate cover, and no more than two members of any single department may be on leave simultaneously. Requests are considered in the order received.

Warehouse staff who are rostered to work on a bank holiday receive a day in lieu, to be taken within three months.

---

[GEN-01#004] Company Overview > Leave year; Trading history (v1.4, effective 2026-01-15)
The company leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Entitlement is pro-rated for anyone joining part way through it.

---

[HR-01#003] Annual Leave Policy > Carry over (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
Up to five days may be carried into the following leave year. Carried days must be taken by 30 June or they are lost. Carry-over above five days requires written approval from the department head and is granted only where leave could not be taken for operational reasons.

---

[HR-01#001] Annual Leave Policy > Entitlement (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
All permanent full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per leave year, in addition to the 8 English bank holidays. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on contracted hours.

Employees with five or more years of continuous service receive one additional day per completed year, to a maximum of 30 days.

---

[HR-06#002] Training and Development > Professional development; Study leave; Availability during training (v1.2, effective 2025-04-01)
Each employee has an annual development conversation with their line manager in April, following the performance review cycle.

The company will consider funding professional qualifications relevant to the employee's role. Applications are made to the People team with a supporting business case from the line manager. Funding above £1,500 requires Managing Director approval.

QUESTION: My RA number was issued 18 days ago. Can I still use it?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [OPS-02#002], a Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Since your RA number was issued 18 days ago, which exceeds the 14-day validity period, you cannot use it.

EVIDENCE:
[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[OPS-02#002] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Receipt; Inspection; Carriage (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
Returned parcels are booked in at the goods-in desk against the RA number on the same day they arrive. Parcels without a visible RA number are quarantined in the returns cage and Customer Services is notified.

A returns operative inspects each item within two working days of receipt and assigns a disposition:

| Disposition | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| A | As new, resaleable | Return to stock |
| B | Opened, undamaged | Return to stock, flag for discount channel |
| C | Damaged or used | Do not restock, photograph, quarantine |
| D | Faulty within warranty | Photograph, route to supplier claim under CS-03 |

Every disposition is recorded against the RA number with the operative's initials.

Where the return is due to company error or a faulty item, the company pays return carriage. Otherwise the customer pays.

---

[IT-01#004] Password and Access Policy > Leavers; Shared and generic accounts (v1.4, effective 2024-06-01) [SUPERSEDED, replaced by IT-11]
The People team notifies IT of every leaver at least five working days before the final working day, or immediately in the case of summary dismissal. Accounts are disabled at the end of the final working day, not deleted, and are retained in a disabled state for 90 days before removal.

Shared accounts are not permitted except for the warehouse scanner accounts, which are tied to a device rather than a person. These have no access to personal data and cannot approve transactions.

---

---

[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

Journeys between home and the normal place of work are not claimable. Where an employee travels from home directly to a customer site, the claimable distance is the lesser of the actual journey and the journey from the office.

QUESTION: How quickly must I report a lost company laptop?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
You must report a lost company laptop to the IT helpdesk within 1 hour of becoming aware [IT-03#001].

EVIDENCE:
[IT-03#001] Security Incident Reporting > What counts as an incident (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Report any of the following:

- A lost or stolen laptop, phone or USB device
- An email sent to the wrong recipient containing personal or confidential data
- Clicking a link or opening an attachment in a suspected phishing email
- Suspected malware, ransomware or unexpected system behaviour
- Unauthorised access to a system, room or filing cabinet
- Paper records lost, or found where they should not be
- Any suspicion that a password has been compromised

If you are unsure whether something is an incident, report it. Reporting something harmless costs a few minutes; not reporting a real breach can cost the company a great deal more.

---

[IT-03#002] Security Incident Reporting > How to report; Timescales (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Telephone the IT helpdesk on extension 4040 immediately, and follow up by email to ithelp@northgate-kitchenware.invalid. Do not attempt to fix or investigate the problem yourself, and do not delete anything, as evidence may be needed.

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Report to IT helpdesk | Within 1 hour of becoming aware |
| IT initial assessment | Within 4 hours |
| Notify Data Protection Lead if personal data is involved | Within 24 hours |
| Notify the ICO if the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights | Within 72 hours of the company becoming aware |
| Notify affected individuals if the risk is high | Without undue delay |

---

[GEN-04#003] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Responsibilities (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment remains the property of Northgate Kitchenware Ltd. Staff are responsible for its reasonable care. Loss or theft must be reported to the IT helpdesk within 24 hours and, if the device held company data, this also triggers the security incident procedure in IT-03.

Personal use of company equipment is permitted within reason. Installing unlicensed software, disabling security software, or allowing family members to use a company device are not permitted.

---

[IT-02#003] Data Protection and Information Handling > Reporting a suspected breach; Access review (v2.0, effective 2025-11-01)
A suspected personal data breach is reported to the Data Protection Lead within 24 hours of discovery, whether or not it is later confirmed.

Access to systems holding personal data is reviewed annually by the Data Protection Lead. Managers confirm in writing that every account in their area is still required.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[IT-04#004] Backup and Recovery > Testing; Requesting a restore (v1.3, effective 2025-05-01)
A restore test is performed quarterly. One system is chosen at random, restored to an isolated environment, and verified. Results are recorded and reported to the senior team. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup.

Staff who need a deleted file recovered contact the IT helpdesk. Files deleted within the last 30 days can normally be recovered the same working day.

QUESTION: How long do I have to return an unwanted item?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
You can return an unwanted item within 28 days of delivery, provided it is unused and in its original packaging. [CS-03#001]

EVIDENCE:
[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

---

[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[CS-02#003] Damaged Goods Frequently Asked Questions > What happens next? (v1.5, effective 2025-12-01)
Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.

Customer services raise a damage report and offer, at the customer's choice, a replacement despatched within one working day of the report being accepted, or a refund processed under OPS-03.

Damaged items are collected by the carrier or, for low-value items, the customer is asked to dispose of them. Do not return a damaged item without a Returns Authorisation number.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[OPS-03#001] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Scope (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

| Route | Basis | Inspection first? |
|---|---|---|
| Statutory cancellation | Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 | No. The deadline runs from receipt of the goods or from the customer's evidence of dispatch, whichever is earlier, so a refund may fall due before inspection is complete. |
| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews each entry within five working days [REG-01#005].

[REG-01#005] Health and Safety Policy > Accident records; Monitoring (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
All accidents, injuries and near misses are recorded in the accident book. The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews each entry within five working days and determines whether it is reportable to the Health and Safety Executive.

The Health and Safety Coordinator conducts a documented site inspection monthly. Findings and outstanding actions are reported to the senior team. An external health and safety consultant audits the site annually.

---

[OPS-08#004] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Escalation; Investigation (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews every entry within two working days and decides whether it is reportable under RIDDOR 2013.

| Category | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Death or specified injury | Report to HSE without delay, then within 10 days |
| Over-seven-day incapacitation | Report within 15 days |
| Dangerous occurrence | Report without delay, then within 10 days |
| Occupational disease | Report on diagnosis |

Any accident causing injury, and any near miss with the potential to cause serious injury, is investigated by the Health and Safety Coordinator with the relevant supervisor. Findings and corrective actions are reported to the senior team monthly.

---

[REG-01#003] Health and Safety Policy > Risk assessment (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Risk assessments are completed for all significant activities, reviewed annually, and reviewed immediately following an accident, a near miss, or a change to the activity. Assessments are held in the warehouse office and on the shared drive.

Specific assessments cover manual handling, workplace transport, working at height, display screen equipment, COSHH, and new and expectant mothers.

---

[REG-01#004] Health and Safety Policy > Consultation; Key procedures (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Safety matters are a standing item at the monthly team briefing. Employees may raise concerns directly with the Health and Safety Coordinator or anonymously through the suggestion box at reception.

Fire evacuation is covered in OPS-07, first aid and accident reporting in OPS-08, warehouse rules in OPS-05, and forklift operation in OPS-06.

---

[OPS-08#003] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Reporting (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
Every accident, injury and near miss must be recorded in the accident book held in the warehouse office, on the same day wherever possible. This includes incidents involving visitors and contractors, and incidents where no injury resulted.

Near misses are reported because they identify hazards before someone is hurt. There is no blame attached to reporting one.

---

A suspected personal data breach is reported to the Data Protection Lead within 24 hours of discovery, whether or not it is later confirmed.

Access to systems holding personal data is reviewed annually by the Data Protection Lead. Managers confirm in writing that every account in their area is still required.

QUESTION: Can I use washing-up liquid when washing by hand?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [PRD-02#002], a small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan.

EVIDENCE:
[PRD-02#002] Cast Iron Care Guide > Everyday washing (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

[PRD-02#003] Cast Iron Care Guide > Stuck-on food; Rust (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Simmer a little water in the pan for a few minutes and scrape with a wooden spatula, or scour with coarse salt and a paper towel. Do not soak.

Rust is not a fault and is not covered by warranty. Scour the rust off with steel wool, wash, dry, and re-season from bare metal.

---

[PRD-01#004] Knife Care Guide > Storage; Stainless and carbon steel (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[PRD-02#001] Cast Iron Care Guide > Seasoning (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Seasoning is a layer of polymerised oil bonded to the iron. It gives the non-stick surface and protects against rust. It is built up, not applied once.

To season: wash and dry thoroughly, apply a very thin coat of a high smoke point oil such as rapeseed or grapeseed, wipe out until the surface looks dry, then bake upside down at 220°C for one hour with a tray beneath. Let it cool in the oven. Repeat two or three times for a new or stripped pan.

Too much oil is the most common mistake. It leaves a sticky, patchy surface rather than a hard one.

QUESTION: Is detergent safe on my cookware?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [PRD-02#002], a small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned cast iron pan, but modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. There is no specific mention of detergent safety for other types of cookware.

EVIDENCE:
[PRD-02#002] Cast Iron Care Guide > Everyday washing (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-02#004] Cast Iron Care Guide > What not to cook; Enamelled cast iron (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Highly acidic foods such as tomato sauce and wine reductions will strip a young seasoning if simmered for a long time. A well-established seasoning tolerates them.

Enamelled pans are not seasoned and must not be. Avoid thermal shock: never put a hot enamelled pan into cold water, as the enamel will craze.

---

[PRD-02#001] Cast Iron Care Guide > Seasoning (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Seasoning is a layer of polymerised oil bonded to the iron. It gives the non-stick surface and protects against rust. It is built up, not applied once.

To season: wash and dry thoroughly, apply a very thin coat of a high smoke point oil such as rapeseed or grapeseed, wipe out until the surface looks dry, then bake upside down at 220°C for one hour with a tray beneath. Let it cool in the oven. Repeat two or three times for a new or stripped pan.

Too much oil is the most common mistake. It leaves a sticky, patchy surface rather than a hard one.

---

[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

[REG-01#001] Health and Safety Policy > Statement of intent (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Northgate Kitchenware Ltd is committed to providing a safe and healthy working environment for employees, contractors, visitors and anyone affected by its activities, so far as is reasonably practicable. This policy is reviewed annually and is signed by the Managing Director.

The company has five or more employees, so this policy is written down as required by the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

---

[PRD-01#004] Knife Care Guide > Storage; Stainless and carbon steel (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.

QUESTION: Is detergent safe on my cookware?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [PRD-02#002], a small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned cast iron pan, but modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use.

EVIDENCE:
[PRD-02#002] Cast Iron Care Guide > Everyday washing (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

QUESTION: Should I use soap on a pan or a knife?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
According to [PRD-02#002], for cast iron pans, "A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan". There is no mention of using soap on knives.

EVIDENCE:
[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

[PRD-01#003] Knife Care Guide > Sharpening and honing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Honing with a steel realigns an edge that has rolled and should be done every few uses. It does not remove metal and does not sharpen.

Sharpening removes metal and restores the edge. A whetstone gives the best result. For most European knives, sharpen at 20 degrees per side; for Japanese knives, 15 degrees per side. Pull-through sharpeners are convenient but remove more metal than necessary and shorten the life of a good knife.

Sharpen when the knife no longer slices a tomato skin cleanly under its own weight.

---

[PRD-01#002] Knife Care Guide > Cutting surfaces (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Use wood or plastic boards. Glass, marble, stone and ceramic boards will blunt an edge within a few cuts and can chip it. Do not cut on a plate, and do not use the blade to scrape the board, as this rolls the edge; turn the knife over and use the spine.

---

[PRD-01#004] Knife Care Guide > Storage; Stainless and carbon steel (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.

---

[PRD-02#002] Cast Iron Care Guide > Everyday washing (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-02#003] Cast Iron Care Guide > Stuck-on food; Rust (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Simmer a little water in the pan for a few minutes and scrape with a wooden spatula, or scour with coarse salt and a paper towel. Do not soak.

Rust is not a fault and is not covered by warranty. Scour the rust off with steel wool, wash, dry, and re-season from bare metal.

[HR-01#002] Annual Leave Policy > Leave year; Booking (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March.

Leave is requested through the People system at least two weeks before the intended start date for absences of up to five days, and at least six weeks before for longer absences. Requests are approved by the line manager.

Approval is not automatic. Managers must maintain adequate cover, and no more than two members of any single department may be on leave simultaneously. Requests are considered in the order received.

---

[HR-01#004] Annual Leave Policy > Bank holidays; Leaving the company (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
Warehouse staff who are rostered to work on a bank holiday receive a day in lieu, to be taken within three months.

On termination, any accrued but untaken leave is paid in the final salary payment. Leave taken in excess of the accrued entitlement is deducted from final pay.

---

[GEN-01#004] Company Overview > Leave year; Trading history (v1.4, effective 2026-01-15)
The company leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Entitlement is pro-rated for anyone joining part way through it.

Turnover for the year ending 31 March 2026 was £8.2 million. The company has traded profitably every year since 2014.

---

[HR-01#003] Annual Leave Policy > Carry over (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
Up to five days may be carried into the following leave year. Carried days must be taken by 30 June or they are lost. Carry-over above five days requires written approval from the department head and is granted only where leave could not be taken for operational reasons.

---

[HR-01#001] Annual Leave Policy > Entitlement (v3.0, effective 2026-04-01)
All permanent full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per leave year, in addition to the 8 English bank holidays. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on contracted hours.

Employees with five or more years of continuous service receive one additional day per completed year, to a maximum of 30 days.

---

[HR-06#002] Training and Development > Professional development; Study leave; Availability during training (v1.2, effective 2025-04-01)
Each employee has an annual development conversation with their line manager in April, following the performance review cycle.

The company will consider funding professional qualifications relevant to the employee's role. Applications are made to the People team with a supporting business case from the line manager. Funding above £1,500 requires Managing Director approval.

Where the company funds a qualification costing more than £1,000, the employee signs a training agreement requiring repayment on a sliding scale if they leave within two years of completion.

Up to five days of paid study leave per year may be granted for company-funded qualifications, at the line manager's discretion.

Employees attending training remain contactable during core hours of 10:00 to 16:30 unless the course makes that impossible.

QUESTION: How long is a Returns Authorisation number valid for?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue [OPS-03#002].

EVIDENCE:
[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

---

[OPS-03#004] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Amount; Authorisation (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
The refund covers the price paid for the goods. Original outbound delivery is refunded where the customer is exercising a statutory cancellation right or where the goods were faulty, and is not refunded for a discretionary change-of-mind return.

Where disposition B has been recorded on a discretionary change-of-mind return, a deduction may be applied for the actual reduction in value caused by the customer handling the goods beyond what is necessary to establish their nature and function. The deduction must reflect the assessed diminished value, not a fixed percentage, must be evidenced by the disposition record, and must be explained to the customer before it is applied. No deduction is made where the customer is exercising a statutory cancellation right and has handled the goods no more than they would in a shop.

| Refund value | Authorised by |
|---|---|
| Up to £250 | Customer Services advisor |
| £251 to £1,000 | Customer Services Manager |
| Above £1,000 | Finance Manager |

---

[OPS-02#002] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Receipt; Inspection; Carriage (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
Returned parcels are booked in at the goods-in desk against the RA number on the same day they arrive. Parcels without a visible RA number are quarantined in the returns cage and Customer Services is notified.

A returns operative inspects each item within two working days of receipt and assigns a disposition:

| Disposition | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| A | As new, resaleable | Return to stock |
| B | Opened, undamaged | Return to stock, flag for discount channel |
| C | Damaged or used | Do not restock, photograph, quarantine |
| D | Faulty within warranty | Photograph, route to supplier claim under CS-03 |

Every disposition is recorded against the RA number with the operative's initials.

Where the return is due to company error or a faulty item, the company pays return carriage. Otherwise the customer pays.

---

[OPS-03#001] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Scope (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

| Route | Basis | Inspection first? |
|---|---|---|
| Statutory cancellation | Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 | No. The deadline runs from receipt of the goods or from the customer's evidence of dispatch, whichever is earlier, so a refund may fall due before inspection is complete. |
| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

QUESTION: How long is a Returns Authorisation number valid for?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue [OPS-03#002].

EVIDENCE:
[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

---

[OPS-03#004] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Amount; Authorisation (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
The refund covers the price paid for the goods. Original outbound delivery is refunded where the customer is exercising a statutory cancellation right or where the goods were faulty, and is not refunded for a discretionary change-of-mind return.

Where disposition B has been recorded on a discretionary change-of-mind return, a deduction may be applied for the actual reduction in value caused by the customer handling the goods beyond what is necessary to establish their nature and function. The deduction must reflect the assessed diminished value, not a fixed percentage, must be evidenced by the disposition record, and must be explained to the customer before it is applied. No deduction is made where the customer is exercising a statutory cancellation right and has handled the goods no more than they would in a shop.

| Refund value | Authorised by |
|---|---|
| Up to £250 | Customer Services advisor |
| £251 to £1,000 | Customer Services Manager |
| Above £1,000 | Finance Manager |

---

[OPS-02#002] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Receipt; Inspection; Carriage (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
Returned parcels are booked in at the goods-in desk against the RA number on the same day they arrive. Parcels without a visible RA number are quarantined in the returns cage and Customer Services is notified.

A returns operative inspects each item within two working days of receipt and assigns a disposition:

| Disposition | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| A | As new, resaleable | Return to stock |
| B | Opened, undamaged | Return to stock, flag for discount channel |
| C | Damaged or used | Do not restock, photograph, quarantine |
| D | Faulty within warranty | Photograph, route to supplier claim under CS-03 |

Every disposition is recorded against the RA number with the operative's initials.

Where the return is due to company error or a faulty item, the company pays return carriage. Otherwise the customer pays.

---

[OPS-03#001] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Scope (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

| Route | Basis | Inspection first? |
|---|---|---|

| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

|---|---|

QUESTION: What is the mileage rate for business travel?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
The mileage rate for business travel is 55 pence per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year, and 25 pence per mile thereafter. [HR-13#001]

EVIDENCE:
[HR-13#001] Expenses Policy > Mileage (v2.0, effective 2026-04-01)
This policy replaces HR-03 with effect from 1 April 2026.

Employees using a private vehicle for business travel may claim 55 pence per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year, and 25 pence per mile thereafter. These rates match the HMRC approved mileage allowance payment rates that took effect on 6 April 2026, so no tax liability arises and no Mileage Allowance Relief is due.

Journeys between home and the normal place of work are not claimable. Where an employee travels from home directly to a customer site, the claimable distance is the lesser of the actual journey and the journey from the office.

---

> This version has been withdrawn. See HR-13 for the policy in force.

Employees using a private vehicle for business travel may claim 40 pence per mile. Journeys between home and the normal place of work are not claimable.

| Circumstance | Limit |
|---|---|
| Breakfast, where travel begins before 06:00 | £6 |
| Lunch, where away from site for more than 5 hours | £8 |
| Evening meal, where returning after 20:00 | £18 |

Alcohol is not reimbursed.

---

[HR-13#003] Expenses Policy > Accommodation (v2.0, effective 2026-04-01)
Hotel accommodation is capped at £130 per night outside London and £170 per night within the M25. Bookings must be made through the company travel portal. Where the cap cannot be met, prior approval from the department head is required.

---

[HR-03#002] Expenses Policy > Accommodation; Submission (v1.3, effective 2024-04-01) [SUPERSEDED, replaced by HR-13]
Hotel accommodation is capped at £110 per night outside London and £140 per night within the M25. Bookings must be made through the nominated travel agent wherever possible.

Claims are submitted on the paper expenses form with original receipts attached, and must reach Finance within 60 days of the expenditure. Claims are reimbursed with the following month's salary.

---

[GEN-01#003] Company Overview > Who we sell to; Structure (v1.4, effective 2026-01-15)
Roughly 70% of revenue comes from trade customers: independent restaurants, cafes, catering companies and small hotel groups, predominantly within a 60-mile radius of the site. The remaining 30% is direct-to-consumer through the online store.

The company has six departments: Sales, Customer Services, Warehouse and Logistics, Finance, IT, and People. Each department head reports to the Managing Director. The senior team meets weekly on Monday mornings.

---

[CS-11#002] Delivery Frequently Asked Questions > What does delivery cost? (v2.2, effective 2026-02-01)
| Service | Cost, excluding VAT |
|---|---|
| Standard, orders under £75 | £6.95 |
| Standard, orders £75 and over | Free |
| Next working day | £12.95 |
| Pre-noon next working day | £19.95 |
| Highlands, islands and Northern Ireland | £14.95, 3 to 7 working days |

Free delivery applies to the goods value excluding VAT and excluding any surcharge postcodes.

- Clicking a link or opening an attachment in a suspected phishing email
- Suspected malware, ransomware or unexpected system behaviour
- Unauthorised access to a system, room or filing cabinet

- Any suspicion that a password has been compromised

QUESTION: How long do I have to return an unwanted item?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
You can return an unwanted item within 28 days of delivery, provided it is unused and in its original packaging. [CS-03#001]

EVIDENCE:
[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

---

[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[CS-02#003] Damaged Goods Frequently Asked Questions > What happens next? (v1.5, effective 2025-12-01)
Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.

Customer services raise a damage report and offer, at the customer's choice, a replacement despatched within one working day of the report being accepted, or a refund processed under OPS-03.

Damaged items are collected by the carrier or, for low-value items, the customer is asked to dispose of them. Do not return a damaged item without a Returns Authorisation number.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[OPS-03#001] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Scope (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

| Route | Basis | Inspection first? |
|---|---|---|
| Statutory cancellation | Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 | No. The deadline runs from receipt of the goods or from the customer's evidence of dispatch, whichever is earlier, so a refund may fall due before inspection is complete. |
| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

[CS-03#001] Warranty Frequently Asked Questions > How long do I have to return an item?; What warranty do you offer? (v1.9, effective 2026-01-01)
Unwanted items may be returned within 28 days of delivery provided they are unused and in their original packaging. This is separate from a warranty claim, which may be made at any point during the warranty period.

| Use | Warranty period |
|---|---|
| Domestic use | 2 years from date of delivery |
| Commercial or catering use | 1 year from date of delivery |

Some manufacturers offer longer cover on specific ranges, stated on the product page. Where the manufacturer's warranty is longer, it applies.

The warranty is in addition to statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which are not affected by it.

---

[OPS-02#001] Returns Standard Operating Procedure > Scope; Return authorisation (v2.3, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

---

[OPS-03#002] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Authorisation validity; Timing (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
A Returns Authorisation number is valid for 14 days from issue. Refunds are not processed against an expired number.

| Customer type | Refund issued within |
|---|---|
| Consumer, statutory cancellation | 14 days of receiving the goods back, or of the customer supplying evidence that they have sent them, whichever is earlier |
| Consumer, standard 30-day return | 10 working days of disposition |
| Trade account | Credit note within 5 working days of disposition |

---

[CS-02#003] Damaged Goods Frequently Asked Questions > What happens next? (v1.5, effective 2025-12-01)
Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.

Customer services raise a damage report and offer, at the customer's choice, a replacement despatched within one working day of the report being accepted, or a refund processed under OPS-03.

Damaged items are collected by the carrier or, for low-value items, the customer is asked to dispose of them. Do not return a damaged item without a Returns Authorisation number.

---

[GEN-04#004] IT Equipment Issue and Return > Returns (v1.1, effective 2025-11-01)
Equipment must be returned to the IT helpdesk on the final working day of employment or when changing to a role with a different allocation. IT wipes and re-images all returned devices before reissue. Devices more than four years old are securely disposed of through a certified recycling contractor, and a destruction certificate is retained.

---

[OPS-03#001] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Scope (v1.4, effective 2025-12-01)
This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

| Route | Basis | Inspection first? |
|---|---|---|
| Statutory cancellation | Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 | No. The deadline runs from receipt of the goods or from the customer's evidence of dispatch, whichever is earlier, so a refund may fall due before inspection is complete. |
| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

QUESTION: How long does the Health and Safety Coordinator have to review an accident book entry?

ANSWER UNDER REVIEW:
The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews each entry within five working days [REG-01#005].

EVIDENCE:
[REG-01#005] Health and Safety Policy > Accident records; Monitoring (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
All accidents, injuries and near misses are recorded in the accident book. The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews each entry within five working days and determines whether it is reportable to the Health and Safety Executive.

The Health and Safety Coordinator conducts a documented site inspection monthly. Findings and outstanding actions are reported to the senior team. An external health and safety consultant audits the site annually.

---

[OPS-08#004] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Escalation; Investigation (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews every entry within two working days and decides whether it is reportable under RIDDOR 2013.

| Category | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Death or specified injury | Report to HSE without delay, then within 10 days |
| Over-seven-day incapacitation | Report within 15 days |
| Dangerous occurrence | Report without delay, then within 10 days |
| Occupational disease | Report on diagnosis |

Any accident causing injury, and any near miss with the potential to cause serious injury, is investigated by the Health and Safety Coordinator with the relevant supervisor. Findings and corrective actions are reported to the senior team monthly.

---

[REG-01#003] Health and Safety Policy > Risk assessment (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Risk assessments are completed for all significant activities, reviewed annually, and reviewed immediately following an accident, a near miss, or a change to the activity. Assessments are held in the warehouse office and on the shared drive.

Specific assessments cover manual handling, workplace transport, working at height, display screen equipment, COSHH, and new and expectant mothers.

---

[REG-01#004] Health and Safety Policy > Consultation; Key procedures (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Safety matters are a standing item at the monthly team briefing. Employees may raise concerns directly with the Health and Safety Coordinator or anonymously through the suggestion box at reception.

Fire evacuation is covered in OPS-07, first aid and accident reporting in OPS-08, warehouse rules in OPS-05, and forklift operation in OPS-06.

---

[OPS-08#003] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Reporting (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
Every accident, injury and near miss must be recorded in the accident book held in the warehouse office, on the same day wherever possible. This includes incidents involving visitors and contractors, and incidents where no injury resulted.

Near misses are reported because they identify hazards before someone is hurt. There is no blame attached to reporting one.

---

[IT-02#003] Data Protection and Information Handling > Reporting a suspected breach; Access review (v2.0, effective 2025-11-01)
A suspected personal data breach is reported to the Data Protection Lead within 24 hours of discovery, whether or not it is later confirmed.

Access to systems holding personal data is reviewed annually by the Data Protection Lead. Managers confirm in writing that every account in their area is still required.

Every accident, injury and near miss must be recorded in the accident book held in the warehouse office, on the same day wherever possible. This includes incidents involving visitors and contractors, and incidents where no injury resulted.

Near misses are reported because they identify hazards before someone is hurt. There is no blame attached to reporting one.

---

[REG-01#005] Health and Safety Policy > Accident records; Monitoring (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)

The Health and Safety Coordinator conducts a documented site inspection monthly. Findings and outstanding actions are reported to the senior team. An external health and safety consultant audits the site annually.

---

[OPS-08#004] First Aid and Accident Reporting > Escalation; Investigation (v2.1, effective 2025-09-01)
The Health and Safety Coordinator reviews every entry within two working days and decides whether it is reportable under RIDDOR 2013.

|---|---|
| Death or specified injury | Report to HSE without delay, then within 10 days |
| Over-seven-day incapacitation | Report within 15 days |
| Dangerous occurrence | Report without delay, then within 10 days |
| Occupational disease | Report on diagnosis |

---

Risk assessments are completed for all significant activities, reviewed annually, and reviewed immediately following an accident, a near miss, or a change to the activity. Assessments are held in the warehouse office and on the shared drive.

---

Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.

Customer services raise a damage report and offer, at the customer's choice, a replacement despatched within one working day of the report being accepted, or a refund processed under OPS-03.

Damaged items are collected by the carrier or, for low-value items, the customer is asked to dispose of them. Do not return a damaged item without a Returns Authorisation number.

---

[IT-03#003] Security Incident Reporting > No blame; Records (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Staff who report their own mistakes promptly and honestly will not face disciplinary action for the mistake itself. Concealing an incident, or failing to report one, may be treated as misconduct.

All incidents are recorded in the incident log, whether or not they are reportable to the ICO. The log is reviewed quarterly by the senior team.

Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

---

Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Simmer a little water in the pan for a few minutes and scrape with a wooden spatula, or scour with coarse salt and a paper towel. Do not soak.

Wash by hand with hot water and a stiff brush while the pan is still warm. A small amount of washing-up liquid is fine on a well-seasoned pan; the modern detergents that would strip seasoning are no longer in common use. Never put cast iron in a dishwasher.

Dry immediately and completely, on a low hob ring if necessary, then wipe a trace of oil over the cooking surface.

---

[PRD-02#004] Cast Iron Care Guide > What not to cook; Enamelled cast iron (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Highly acidic foods such as tomato sauce and wine reductions will strip a young seasoning if simmered for a long time. A well-established seasoning tolerates them.

Enamelled pans are not seasoned and must not be. Avoid thermal shock: never put a hot enamelled pan into cold water, as the enamel will craze.

---

[PRD-02#001] Cast Iron Care Guide > Seasoning (v1.2, effective 2025-06-01)
Seasoning is a layer of polymerised oil bonded to the iron. It gives the non-stick surface and protects against rust. It is built up, not applied once.

To season: wash and dry thoroughly, apply a very thin coat of a high smoke point oil such as rapeseed or grapeseed, wipe out until the surface looks dry, then bake upside down at 220°C for one hour with a tray beneath. Let it cool in the oven. Repeat two or three times for a new or stripped pan.

Too much oil is the most common mistake. It leaves a sticky, patchy surface rather than a hard one.

---

[PRD-01#001] Knife Care Guide > Washing (v1.3, effective 2025-06-01)
Wash knives by hand in warm soapy water and dry immediately. Dishwashers damage knives in three ways: the detergent is abrasive and dulls the edge, the heat can loosen or crack handle scales, and blades knocking against other items chip the edge. Dishwasher damage is not covered by the warranty described in CS-03.

Never leave a knife soaking in a sink. It damages the handle and it is a serious cutting hazard for the next person.

---

[REG-01#001] Health and Safety Policy > Statement of intent (v3.2, effective 2026-01-01)
Northgate Kitchenware Ltd is committed to providing a safe and healthy working environment for employees, contractors, visitors and anyone affected by its activities, so far as is reasonably practicable. This policy is reviewed annually and is signed by the Managing Director.

The company has five or more employees, so this policy is written down as required by the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

---

Store in a knife block, on a magnetic strip, or in an edge guard. Loose in a drawer, blades knock together and chip.

Stainless resists rust but is not rustproof; dry it. Carbon steel takes a keener edge and holds it longer, but will rust within hours if left wet, and will develop a dark patina with use. The patina is normal and protective. Rust is not covered by the warranty.
